CVE-2026-40021: Apache Log4net: Silent log event loss in XmlLayout and XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J due to unescaped XML 1.0 forbidden characters
 Optional 1
File
src/eShopModernizedMVC/packages.config:10

Explanation

CVE-2026-40021: Apache Log4net: Silent log event loss in XmlLayout and XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J due to unescaped XML 1.0 forbidden characters

Severity: MEDIUM

Apache Log4net's XmlLayout https://logging.apache.org/log4net/manual/configuration/layouts.html#layout-list and XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J https://logging.apache.org/log4net/manual/configuration/layouts.html#layout-list , in versions before 3.3.0, fail to sanitize characters forbidden by the XML 1.0 specification https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#charsets in MDC property keys and values, as well as the identity field that may carry attacker-influenced data. This causes an exception during serialization and the silent loss of the affected log event.

An attacker who can influence any of these fields can exploit this to suppress individual log records, impairing audit trails and detection of malicious activity.

Users are advised to upgrade to Apache Log4net 3.3.0, which fixes this issue.

Affected dependencies:
- log4net:2.0.12 (packages.config:10); range < 3.3.0; patched

Recommended fix: upgrade log4net to 3.3.0 or later.

Explanation

CVE-2024-21319: Microsoft ASP.NET Core project templates vulnerable to denial of service

Severity: MEDIUM

A Denial of Service vulnerability exists in ASP.NET Core project templates which utilize JWT-based authentication tokens. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated client to consume arbitrarily large amounts of server memory, potentially triggering an out-of-memory condition on the server and making the server no longer able to respond to legitimate requests.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/290

### Mitigation factors

This impacts only .NET Core-based projects that were created using any version of project templates listed in affected software.
Other project templates e.g., console applications, MAUI applications, Windows Forms or WPF applications, are not affected.

## Affected software

This impacts only .NET Core-based projects that were created using any version of the below project templates.

  • ASP.NET Core Web App (Model-View-Controller)
  • ASP.NET Core Web API
  • ASP.NET Core Web App (Razor Pages)
  • Blazor Server App
  • Blazor WebAssembly App

## Advisory FAQ

### How do I know if I am affected?

If you are you using project templates listed in affected software, you may be exposed to the vulnerability.

### How do I fix the issue?

#### For existing projects:
If you ever created any of these projects via the dotnet new command or via Visual Studio's File -> New Project gesture, and if you enabled federated authentication at project creation time, your project may be vulnerable. To remediate the vulnerability, use your package manager to update any references you may have to the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect, and Microsoft.IdentityModel.JsonWebTokens packages to their respective latest versions.

  • Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer
  • Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect

If your project does not reference any of those three packages, you are not exposed to this vulnerability.

#### For new projects:
To remediate this issue please update to the latest SDK listed below. Simply installing the SDK update is not sufficient to remediate projects already-created / already-deployed projects which existed prior to this update being released.

  • To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET 6.0 or .NET 7.0. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs.
  • If you are using one of the affected packages, please update to the patched version listed above.
  • If you have .NET 6.0 or greater installed, you can list the versions you have installed by running the dotnet --info command. You will see output like the following;

  • If you're using .NET 7.0, you should download and install .NET SDK 7.0.115 (for Visual Studio 2022 v17.4) from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/7.0.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed self-contained applications targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

Architecture Diagram

The workspace contains a single ASP.NET MVC catalog application. It runs with either a mock catalog or Entity Framework-backed SQL Server storage, and can optionally use Azure identity, blob storage, and Application Insights.

Data Storage & External Services

The catalog is stored in SQL Server through Entity Framework when UseMockData is false; otherwise the application uses an in-memory mock service. Product images can be stored in Azure Blob Storage, and Azure Active Directory and Application Insights are configured as optional integrations. Redis session support is referenced by a package but its session configuration is commented out.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • The application is a single MVC deployment with controllers, services, and an EF6 context registered through Autofac.
  • Configuration flags select mock or database catalog storage, local or Azure image storage, and local or managed-identity SQL authentication.
  • MVC actions render Razor views; no separate API gateway or independently deployable business service is present.

API & Service Communication Contracts

The application exposes MVC page and form actions, plus one image-upload action. The application uses synchronous in-process service calls and SQL/blob SDK operations; no independent REST services or message broker were discovered.

DTOs & Contracts

CatalogItem is the MVC form and domain model used for create, edit, details, and list responses. CatalogBrand and CatalogType are related catalog models. PaginatedItemsViewModel wraps page metadata and catalog results. The image-upload action returns an anonymous JSON contract containing a name and URL. No OpenAPI document, protobuf schema, GraphQL schema, or separate gateway-level DTO was found. MVC model binding and the default JSON serialization behavior are used.

Communication Patterns

  • Controller-to-service and service-to-context calls are synchronous in-process calls. EF6 executes SQL Server operations; the Azure Storage SDK performs optional blob operations.
  • Authentication uses OWIN cookie and OpenID Connect middleware when Azure AD is enabled. Otherwise, a local middleware supplies an authenticated claims identity; authentication behavior is therefore configuration-dependent.
  • There is no message queue, service discovery, API gateway, explicit retry/circuit-breaker policy, or documented client-side load balancing.
  • Docker Compose declares the web application as depending on sql.data; it does not configure a health-conditioned dependency for application startup.
  • The Compose mapping exposes the container over HTTP. TLS termination is not configured in the project Compose files.
  • The application returns server-rendered MVC views; no separate public REST API was identified.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports browsing and maintaining an online product catalog. It manages catalog items, brands, types, stock thresholds, and product images; no checkout, payment, or order workflow is implemented in this MVC project.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalog ManagementProduct displayed to shoppers and maintained by administratorsBelongs to one CatalogBrand and one CatalogType
CatalogBrandCatalog ManagementBrand classification for productsHas multiple CatalogItem records
CatalogTypeCatalog ManagementProduct type/categoryHas multiple CatalogItem records

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopModernizedMVCCatalog ManagementCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server / EF6; optional Azure Blob Storage; optional Azure AD
CatalogServiceMockCatalog Management mockIn-memory CatalogItem listPreconfigured data

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse the Product Catalog

  1. A shopper requests GET /Catalog/Index, optionally specifying page size and page index.
  2. CatalogController delegates the query to ICatalogService.
  3. The selected implementation loads catalog items and their brand/type associations from EF6/SQL Server, or reads the in-memory mock list.
  4. The controller resolves image URLs through IImageService and returns the paginated Razor view.

Workflow 2: Maintain a Product and Its Image

  1. An authenticated administrator opens the create or edit form.
  2. The browser uploads an image to /uploadimage; PicController decodes the upload and accepts JPEG, PNG, or GIF image formats.
  3. MVC model validation checks the submitted catalog model. The action sets image metadata from the temporary upload response and calls the catalog service.
  4. The service persists the catalog item through EF6, or updates mock data.
  5. When Azure storage is selected, the image service moves the temporary blob into the catalog item's image location; the controller redirects to the catalog.
  6. Delete uses an authenticated POST action to remove a catalog item and then redirects to the list.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There are no business microservices or gateway aggregation flows. The MVC application is the source of truth for catalog metadata and accesses SQL Server directly through EF6. When configured, image bytes flow to Azure Blob Storage while the catalog row retains the image filename. The default mock implementation keeps catalog state in process and does not persist it.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Admin as "Catalog Administrator" participant Browser as "Browser" participant MVC as "MVC Application" participant Pic as "PicController" participant Catalog as "CatalogController" participant Image as "Image Service" participant Service as "Catalog Service" participant DB as "SQL Server" Admin->>Browser: Open catalog create form Browser->>MVC: GET /Catalog/Create MVC->>Catalog: Build form and load brand/type choices Catalog-->>Browser: Create form Admin->>Browser: Select image and product details Browser->>Pic: POST /uploadimage Pic->>Pic: Decode and validate image format alt Image format accepted Pic->>Image: Upload temporary image Image-->>Pic: Temporary image URL Pic-->>Browser: JSON image name and URL Browser->>Catalog: POST /Catalog/Create with product model Catalog->>Catalog: Validate model state Catalog->>Service: Create catalog item Service->>DB: Save catalog row DB-->>Service: Saved item Catalog->>Image: Move temporary image if configured Catalog-->>Browser: Redirect to catalog else Invalid image Pic-->>Browser: 400 Bad Request end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Catalog item names are required. Prices must be within the configured range and use at most two decimal places.
  • Available stock, restock threshold, and maximum stock are constrained to non-negative configured ranges.
  • EF mapping requires each item to reference an existing brand and type.
  • Image upload accepts only decoded JPEG, PNG, or GIF formats. Image storage implementation is selected by configuration.
  • Catalog create, edit, and delete actions use the MVC Authorize attribute. The active authentication behavior depends on whether Azure AD is enabled.
  • EF database initialization creates the catalog schema if needed, creates HiLo sequences, and seeds built-in or optional CSV data.
  • Data changes use EF SaveChanges; no distributed transaction, event bus, saga, or audit trail was found.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The project targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and ASP.NET MVC 5, so moving to modern .NET requires a framework migration rather than a runtime-only update. Several packages are legacy versions; the security scan identified medium-severity advisories for log4net 2.0.12 and JWT-related packages at 5.6.0. Redis session support and Azure integration packages should be reviewed against the intended deployment configuration.

Notable Observations

  • The project uses packages.config and assembly HintPath references rather than SDK-style PackageReference.
  • The package list contains 146 entries but does not indicate which are direct versus transitive.
  • Redis session-state support is installed, but the corresponding sessionState provider configuration is commented out.
  • No test project or test-scoped package set was found in the MVC solution.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The primary data store is SQL Server, accessed through Entity Framework 6. The persistence model consists of catalog items, brands, and types; image bytes are stored separately when Azure Blob Storage is enabled.

Catalog types, brands, and items are seeded from built-in preconfigured data or optional CSV customization files. Sequence definitions are loaded from SQL scripts during initialization. No Flyway/Liquibase or EF migration history workflow was identified.

Entity Model

CatalogDBContext maps the item entity to Catalog, CatalogBrand to CatalogBrand, and CatalogType to CatalogType. An item requires one brand and one type; each brand or type may be associated with multiple catalog items. PictureUri and TempImageName are view/workflow properties and are ignored by EF mapping.

Caching Strategy

No catalog data cache or EF second-level cache was identified. The project includes Microsoft.Web.RedisSessionStateProvider, but the custom Redis session configuration is commented out in Web.config. MVC output caching is configured globally with duration zero and no-store.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The web application is the only service that owns relational catalog data. SQL Server stores catalog metadata; blob storage holds images and is accessed by the image service. No cross-service database access, CQRS split, or event-based data synchronization was found. Mock mode replaces the database service with an in-memory list.
